notes.title: Patch 1.1.8 - Summer Cleaning
notes.content:
[p]Hello! DoubleV here, I've decided to push an update for a number of systems I've been working on along the road to the Nightmare Forge update. It's nothing too major, just a lot of fixes for stat calculations, various crashes and input issues, and fixes to common pain points. Here's the notes![/p]

[h3]1.1.8 - Summer Cleaning[/h3]
[list]
[*]New: Geogem of the Armory - Removes your current artifact and gives you a choice of three others
[*]Changed the way "ground area" indicators detect a cancelled attack, should prevent a lot of "phantom" indicators that would appear when certain enemies were interrupted
[*]Items that are "linked" (disappear when another is taken), now have a visual indicator to show this
[*]Fixed a number of crashes related to orbitals, grappled enemies and a few other things
[*]Fixed a number of issues related to gamepad stick inputs in menus
[*]Fixed certain Geogems requiring the wrong number of held items to activate
[*]Certain artifacts now cannot be used if they would do nothing (Healing when already at full hp, for example)
[*]All tilesets now have a bit of shading to help reduce the contrast of the inner walls, this may change more later
[*]Rewrote the way player stats are calculated behind the scenes. This should fix many issues involving the wrong stats being applied when certain items were picked up/removed under specific conditions, particularly with multipliers
[*]Fixed erroneous stat displays in the pause menu
[*]Fixed a rare softlock with specific player animations
[*]Fixed Gilded Axe visuals displaying incorrectly when enough hitpause was applied (critting an armored enemy, for example)
[*]Made all boss room tilesets larger to keep the camera from clipping out of bounds
[*]Updated the sprite + description for Marketable Plushie
[*]Added a better visual indicator for Atlas's "corner trap" attack
[*]Many fixes to Funky Mushroom and the way it applied random stats on drop/pickup
[*]New particles for Greed Severed, Neurotoxin and Bomb Mark
[*]Scarlett now continues her attack pattern after reforming instead of resetting it
[*]All critical strikes now deal at least 1 extra damage
[/list]

notes.title: Early Access Update 1.11: Scarlet Incursion
notes.content:
Hello again! It's been a few weeks longer than I expected.

Today I'm pleased to announce that the Scarlet Incursion update is finally out! As a smaller update it was initially planned to release last month, but as some of you may have seen on the official DASHPUNCH socials, some technical issues got in the way, among other busyness. With those out of the way, onward to the patch notes!

[h2]Gameplay:[/h2]
[list]
[*]Boss 3 has been rebuilt from the ground up to be more in line with the difficulty curve, at least in terms of attack patterns. I'll likely be tweaking their exact numbers in the coming days/weeks based on feedback, but they should feel a lot more fun to fight now!
[*]There is now an arrow on the right side of the pause screen, that takes you to a new menu to view your current Legacy Upgrades. This should give a better idea of what the upgrade trees look like, as well as keep better track of what you have!
[*]The pause screen now also shows your Artifact information, if you have one.
[*]Added 1 new cursed item: Sniper's Cataract. Find it in Mezztik's shop!
[/list]
[h2]QoL:[/h2]
[list]
[*]A new menu can be found on the title screen, called "Collection". Inside it are two options, "Bestiary" and "Achievements".
[*]The Bestiary gives you a display of every enemy you've defeated across your entire save file. This currently includes the number of kills, and the number of deaths you've had against every enemy in the game! Note that the game hasn't been tracking this until now, so you'll need to play a run after the update to see anything here.
[*]The Achievements menu gives you an in-game way to see what achievements you've collected, which ones are available, and what they've unlocked for you. 
[/list]
[h2]Technical:[/h2]
[list]
[*]Fixed the Rainbow Swirl achievement being automatically unlocked on any hit. Oops!
[*]Bodybullet effects no longer work on invulnerable enemies or bosses.
[*]Fixed some edge cases with hitbox tracking for certain attacks.
[*]Fixed Greedy Claw allowing you to phase through walls. The lunge now stops on contact with a solid object or wall.
[*]Fixed some attacks using the wrong SFX
[*]Fixed many cased of Demon Pact status not being applied to certain projectiles
[*]Fixed some incorrect mouse offsets in the settings menu
[*]Bat on a String will now warp to your location when using the map screen.
[*]Bat on a String will no longer target invulnerable enemies, like worm golem segments.
[*]Fixed Parry not detecting certain hitboxes
[*]Certain values now save to file when exiting a run for any reason (manual exit, dying, ending portal) rather than every time they're updated. Might save a little on performance?
[/list]

[h3]Final Notes: What's next?[/h3]
EA 1.2, for starters! With the current slice of the game being in a more solid spot than ever, I can finally take some time to expand on new content. The next update is a big one, so expect a little bit of everything!
[i]HOWEVER![/i]
It's probably no surprise to hear that the delays with Scarlet Incursion have, in fact, put off the whole schedule I had planned out for the remaining updates; I was already cutting it pretty close without the detours! So I'll cut to the chase: There's gonna be another roadmap update coming soon, and both EA 1.2 and Release 1.0 are getting pushed back a quarter to give me some breathing room. This lands EA 1.2 at Q3 and Release 1.0 at Q3-4, but unlike the previous updates I don't expect these to land at the [i]very end[/i] of those timeframes, and could easily release sooner rather than later. I mostly want to avoid another situation like this one, where an update releases weeks behind schedule due to unplanned circumstances. But I hope you'll look forward to it anyway!

All the best,
-DoubleV

notes.title: Early Access Update 1.1: Mezztik's Marvels
notes.content:
[h1]Mezztik's Marvels is OUT![/h1]
The first of three roadmap updates is finally here, bringing along major QoL changes, new content, new and better visuals, and much much more! As stated in past announcements and the roadmap, Mezztik's Marvels is an update focused on gameplay and systems polish. While that does mean there's no new story chapter, there's still plenty of new content to cover, so let's dive in!
[h2]The Quick Rundown:[/h2]
[list]
[*] A staggering [b]29[/b] new items, very nearly doubling the total item pool
[*] 5 new Chakras to unlock, featuring some much-requested additions to spend those Pact Coins on, along with some changes to a few existing chakras
[*] Over 30 new room layouts!
[*] You can loop runs after beating Scarlett now, if the relevant Chakra is unlocked
[*] A map screen, complete with "fog of war" and fast travel to any room you've visited!
[*] All Chakras can be optionally disabled for more customizability!
[*] A new legacy tree, unlock it's Chakra to wield forbidden magicks!
[*] A new Artifact, freshly refurbished from the early beta days!
[*] A new type of item to find: Cursed items! These are typically not stackable, but provide powerful effects both positive and negative, for a price.
[*] A new character, who deals in Cursed items
[*] A new dialogue system!
[*] Cleaner interface, with better visuals for things like Artifact charge
[*] Enemy pathfinding! They're less stupid now!
[*] Redesigned Geogems! Find them in special rooms called Gem Vaults, and use them to focus your build! There's several new ones, and many of them have been reworked entirely.
[*] Achievements! There's 16 in total, each one unlocking a new item! In the future, these will be one of the primary ways to unlock new content along with Chakras.
[*] Many, [i]many[/i] reworks to everything from items to enemies to status effects to legacies; nearly everything got a balance and design pass, to list them all would probably take up the whole character limit.
[/list]
And for those wanting some more details...
[h2]The Nitty Gritty:[/h2]
[h3]UI/Interface:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Dialogue is now handled with a proper, choice-select menu rather than a simple sequence based on story flags. This means you can revisit special dialogue, as well as see new dialogue highlighted in yellow.
[*] Artifact display tweaked, and will glow when the Artifact is fully charged
[*] A new map screen, that can be accessed whenever you're not in combat. You can click on any room you've visited (highlighted in green) to warp there.
[*] Stats display in the pause menu simplified; Vampirism, Perseverence, Recovery, and Dash Distance removed as they aren't modified by anything anymore.
[*] Fixed a number of issues with UI & camera scaling; all resolutions should have roughly the same vision range now.
[*] Refactored all input handling and control display for better readability and options. You will need to reset your keybinds!
[*] Screenshake is toggleable now, I think the game feels weird without it though
[/list]
[h3]Items & Artifacts:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Artifact charging reworked; all artifacts now charge on room clear, but instead charge over time during timed survival and boss fights
[*] Artifact XP removed, it was mostly a vestigial system from older versions of the game
[*] 1 New Artifact: Greedy Claw
[*] 3 New Common Items: Brass Knuckle, Cockatrice Feather, Overdue Library Book
[*] 2 New Uncommon Items: Red Pistachio, Blue Pistachio
[*] 1 New Rare Item: Attractive Powder
[*] 1 New Ultrarare Item: Gem-Forger Rod
[*] 3 Unlockable Common Items: Worm Weave, Azta's Amplifier, Tack Warts
[*] 4 Unlockable Uncommon Items: Broken Snout Extender, Gream Powder, Rewards Card, Hexplates
[*] 4 Unlockable Rare Items: Valiant, Thunder Tome, Drippy Snowman, Twisted Timer
[*] 2 Unlockable Ultrarare Items: Baphomet Horn, Sunsetter
[*] 3 Unlockable Legendary Items: Stoneheart Bone Smasher, Thumper Boot, Sanctified Concoction
[*] 6 Cursed Items: Doomed Signal (converted from Legendary), Encrusted Dice, Dreamskate, Lucidity, Berserker Rage, Wretched Clown Nose
[*] Redesigned Cursed Blade of Grudges: now marks enemies that damage you, use to slash between all marked enemies.
[*] Redesigned Wave Blaster: Now fires 2 wide projectiles perpendicular to the punch direction on hit.
[*] Redesigned 621-Volt Battery: Charges artifact when a certain number of enemies are destroyed
[*] Redesigned Friendly Leech: Now heals every 10 kills, based on STR
[*] Redesigned Funky Mushroom: Affects fewer stats, but with greater effect.
[*] Many items had damage scaling changed (INT in particular is a bit less centralizing now)
[/list]
[h3]Chakras:[/h3]
[list]
[*] All Chakras can now be disabled by clicking on them again once unlocked. Some effects won't be reset until the next run (starting gold, etc)
[*] Artifact XP Chakras have been replaced, as Artifact XP doesn't exist any more. They now charge your Artifact at specific times.
[*] 5 New Chakras: Donation, Shady Deals, Valued Customer, Recall Self: Warp, Destiny Rejection
[*] Pact Coin drop rate now scales down on a per-room basis, starting at 100% and decreasing by 20% multiplicatively for each Demon-Pact enemy killed (10% during survival phase). This is primarily to prevent items like Doomed Signal from effortlessly snapping the progression over it's knee, it shouldn't make too much of a difference for normal gameplay, and never reaches 0%.
[/list]
[h3]Enemies:[/h3]
[list]
[*] New Enemies: Shotgun Golem, Darkworm, Proto, Architect
[*] Refactored all enemy behaviors, most things should be more consistent now
[*] Enemies will pathfind around walls if they can't see you!
[*] Worm Golem no longer has the Sting property
[*] A few enemies that didn't have attack tells, do now
[*] Stoneheart Tank attack reworked: now lobs a Stoneheart Bomber directly to your location, exploding on impact.
[*] Fixed several inconsisitency issues with angled rectangular hitboxes, primarily affecting Atlas' punches and Wisewood's beams
[*] Atlas' lightning towers are now destructible by hand and don't block movement
[*] Atlas' Thunder Shield damage reduction significantly reduced per tower
[*] Combat rooms will now randomly have "Incursions", spawning a few strong enemies around the room as part of a wave. The chance of this happening increases with Curse.
[*] Redesigned enemy spawn portal visuals to be less obtrusive.
[*] New SFX for a number of enemies.
[/list]
[h3]Geogems:[/h3]
[list]
[*] New Geogems: Power, Mind, Agility, Phantom
[*] Geogem of the Cornerstone buffed: Now gives 1 legendary item for every 5 items lost to its effect
[*] Geogem of Blood effect changed: Sacrifice 50% current HP for +1 STR, DEX, INT
[*] Geogem of the Collective changed: +1 STR if you have 20 or more items, +1 DEX if you have 5 different rarities of items, +1 INT if you have 5 duplicates. Cannot spawn on floor 1.
[*] Geogem of the Soul changed: Now called Geogem of Soulfire, trades 1 INT for full barrier
[*] Geogem of Straights removed
[*] Geogem of Flushes removed
[*] Some Geogems now have a gold price to activate.
[*] Geogem reward distribution slightly tweaked.
[*] Geogems are now tagged based on what aspect of the game they affect; Stats, Items, Buffs, and Funny. The game tries to spawn a relatively even number of each, ensuring that there's always a variety of opportunities available.
[/list]
[h3]Player Character:[/h3]
[list]
[*] All primary stats (STR, DEX, INT) now start at 10. Damage values across the board have been rebalanced to compensate; this prevents an issue where lower starting stats were fundamentally more valuable to increase, because multipliers on them had to be higher.
[*] Vampirism, Perseverence, Recovery, and Dash Distance stats removed, as they were either useless or too difficult to balance.
[*] New Legacy Tree: Warp. Unlocked via Chakra
[/list]
[h3]Miscellaneous Tweaks and Other Things:[/h3]
[list]
[*] A new NPC, who only shows up rarely...
[*] Small ground objects very rarely drop loot when broken
[*] Internally refactored almost all the data in the game, to significantly ease the development of future content.
[*] Renamed the save data file to "PlayerData1.json", from "PlayerData.json" (don't worry, existing data should transfer just fine). This should prevent potential data loss if for some reason you try to play the Demo version after the release version, as well as potentially allowing for multiple files in the future.
[*] Fixed a ton of bugs
[*] Created a ton of bugs (probably)
[/list]
[h3]What's Next For DASHPUNCH?[/h3]
As I mentioned in the last announcement, I'm taking a slight detour away from the roadmap to get some tweaks and content in that were secretly planned for Mezztik's Marvels but didn't [i]quite[/i] make the cut. This should be done sometime next month along with an updated roadmap, and after that I'll be off to start development on EA 1.2, which is still currently unnamed. As always, more to come! And if you made it this far down the notes, just know yours and everyone else's interest is what keeps me going, so a huge thanks for that!

Have fun finding all the new stuff in Mezztik's Marvels!
-DoubleV

notes.title: 2/28 Progress Update, Mezztik's Marvels
notes.content:
Hey all!

It's been awhile since I last posted anything about last year's roadmap (or anything at all, oops), but I'm pleased to say that it's mostly just been a result of being so busy working on it. But rest assured, it is coming, and is currently planned to release sometime next month! I actually planned to make this announcement about a month ago, but as with any of these "soft" tasks, I always find it hard to justify spending time that could otherwise go towards development. Sorry for the dry spell!

Anyway, let's get in to what the Mezztik's Marvels update actually does so far, because it's a long list! And of course, I won't be spoiling *everything*, some of it you'll just have to play and discover on your own.

[h2]Let's dive in![/h2]

Mezztik's Marvels is, at it's core, one part optimization/cleanup and one part content; compared to future updates, this means it's more about quality of life changes, new mechanics, optimization and patching up existing systems than, say, adding new worlds into the main progression. Those will come later! But don't worry, there's still plenty more to do in Mezztik's Marvels alone.

[h3]Backend Rewrites[/h3]
The first big item on the list, just to get the boring stuff out of the way first. This took a huge amount of time and effort, all of January and more in fact. The long and short of it is that previously, DASHPUNCH had no convenient way to store data for things like items, geogems, enemy behaviors, and a host of other things; any data that needed to be associated with, say, an item, was just stored directly in the object itself at runtime. Enemy behaviors were all coded individually for each enemy, with only a small number of shared functions.

Needless to say, this ALL needed to get ripped out and redone if I wanted any hope of future development. So I did! I'll spare the gritty details, but enemies now share most of their code with each other, which is organized into a series of "sub-behaviors" that they can each call as needed. Item and geogem data is also stored much more cleanly now, each one being given an ID that corresponds to their effect scripts and associated text in the lang file, making future translation trivial.

Going forward, adding on to these systems should get MUCH easier!

[h3]Quality of Life Features[/h3]
Along the way, I've also been developing solutions to some of the pain points I've gotten feedback about. (Huge shoutout to anyone who's done that by the way, every bit helps!)

Let's face it, maps in DASHPUNCH get pretty big, and getting around them, trying to remember which rooms you've cleared, where points of interest are, gets tiring and annoying. Enter one of the most requested features: the map screen!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45183822/f935d1c6281f42548b0afbce72cf98907179a606.png[/img]
The map screen is something you can pull up at any time, provided you're not in combat. It displays symbols for every room based on what type of room it is, and whether it's been visited or not! Any previously visited room can also be warped to by clicking the symbol, letting you jump right back to use that Geogem you were saving, or buy new stuff from Vee's shop, anytime!

Speaking of Vee, NPC dialogue has also gotten a lot more robust. Talking with someone now opens up a menu with all of their dialogue options, meaning any special dialogue can be re-read in case you missed something, and makes their interactions with the player feel a lot more organic!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45183822/d647792e0adeb9719b5e7c16e42643369446c1f6.png[/img]
Also not seen here, any unread special dialogue will appear in yellow text!

The Chakra menu has also gotten a notable change; any unlocked Chakras can now also be disabled and re-enabled by clicking them again!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45183822/68e715a86465f36a5599750d968dc921bcda0861.png[/img]
It's a small thing at the end of the day, but it's something I personally like. This allows people to easily set up challenge runs, or disable unwanted help without missing out on any extra content that might be part of the Chakra system. Keep in mind some effects wont be "properly" disabled until the next run though, like starting gold!

There's a host of smaller changes as well: better view scaling for really high or low resolution screens, all-new keybind and control bind glyphs for better readability, new item description boxes that take up less space, and more!

[h3]Geogems, Items and Character Building[/h3]
For all the game's emphasis on picking a Legacy or two and building around it, it turned out there were actually very few ways to do this, since items are totally random, and typically didn't give stats directly. That changes in Mezztik's Marvels!

On top of a ton of item and Geogem effect reworks, Geogems have been divided into a few categories, and spawn in their own room type called a Gem Vault, usually in sets of 3-5. Each Gem Vault makes sure that the Geogems inside have an even spread of gem types; as an example, you'll always find a Geogem that changes your stats somehow. This helps alleviate an issue where the player's build is "stuck", simply because they can't find any way to change it.

Primary stats (STR, DEX, INT), will all start at 10, with all damage sources being readjusted to fit these new values. This fixes an issue were gaining stats that started lower was fundamentally more valuable, making DEX and INT setups quite a bit stronger than intended. In addition, common items now exist to simply raise each of these stats by 1, giving a more clear path towards ramping damage.

Finally, Artifact progression is being reworked; previously, there was a very opaque "artifact experience" system that was left over from super early in development that affected a number of Artifact stats in minor ways. This has been removed, and Artifact stats are now more or less constant. These experience values are still stored in the save data though, and might come up again later for a different system I've been cooking up. Stay tuned!

Of course, on top of these changes is a pile of entirely new items and Geogems as well, including some "cursed" items as mentioned in the roadmap. I'm looking forward to seeing what people do with them! Here's a small teaser you may have seen on the DASHPUNCH Bluesky account:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45183822/8a0459f0854d97ee7b322ea0640ec77bf136f674.jpg[/img]

[h3]Achievements and Unlockables[/h3]
Not everything added in Mezztik's Marvels is given out so freely! Also coming with the update is the first batch of Achievements, ranging from things that will happen by progressing normally, to small little challenges to look out for. These each come with a corresponding Steam Achievement, as well as an unlockable thing for future runs!

[h3]Final Notes[/h3]
Whew, that dragged on a bit longer than I intended. If you actually read all that and made it here, thank you so much! There's still quite a bit I didn't even cover in these notes, but I'm saving those for the full notes once the update releases. But rest assured I'm still hard at work on the update, I haven't died yet. If you want to see more teaser and posts about upcoming content, make sure to follow the DASHPUNCH socials on Bluesky and X.

-DoubleV

notes.title: The "It's not Christmas yet" Patch
notes.content:
[h3]Tha deets[/h3]
[list]
[*]Bosses' demon-pact chance only triggers at 30% curse or higher, and has lower odds than normal
[*]Armor-breaking hit knockback normalized slightly to give better opportunities for followup hits
[*]Dhrystone crit chance now shows on the stats screen properly
[*]Flat damage is now applied after critical modifiers, but before total damage modifiers
[*]Enemy armor regen grace period extended to 1s
[*]Bird projectile slowed and doesn't "slide" on walls anymore
[*]Fixed Cursed Blade of Grudges not displaying the marked target at all
[*]Fixed Geogem of Stability and Geogem of the Mirror sometimes duplicating the wrong item
[*]Fixed Bat on a String bat familiars sticking around even if you lose the item
[/list]
